verses.text: Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth.
Serve the LORD with gladness; come into His presence with joyful songs.
Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture.
Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name.
For the LORD is good, and His loving devotion endures forever; His faithfulness continues to all generations.

context.author: Not named. Book Four (Psalms 90-106) opens with “a prayer of Moses,” and most of its psalms have no title. The Greek Old Testament gives several of them to David, and Hebrews 4:7 quotes Psalm 95 as spoken “through David.”
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship, and the nations called to join
context.setting: The title calls it “A Psalm of thanksgiving,” and it closes the run of songs that began with Psalm 93. “Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth. Serve the LORD with gladness; come into His presence with joyful songs” (vv.1-2). “Know that the LORD is God. It is He who made us, and we are His; we are His people, and the sheep of His pasture” (v.3). “Enter His gates with thanksgiving and His courts with praise; give thanks to Him and bless His name” (v.4). “For the LORD is good, and His loving devotion endures forever; His faithfulness continues to all generations” (v.5).
context.custom: The thanksgiving offering (todah) was a sacrifice brought with bread to thank God for a rescue (Leviticus 7:12-15), and it was eaten in a meal of praise. Worshipers passed through the Temple gates into its courts. “Serve” (v.2) is the word for a servant’s work and for worship. William Kethe’s version of the psalm, ‘All People That on Earth Do Dwell’ (1561), is sung to the tune known as the Old Hundredth.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 101 is David’s vow to lead his house with integrity.
context.timelineBible: Jesus said, “I am the gate” (John 10:9), and “I am the good shepherd. I know My sheep and My sheep know Me” (John 10:14). Paul urged, “Give thanks in every circumstance” (1 Thessalonians 5:18), and Hebrews calls believers to offer God “a sacrifice of praise” (Hebrews 13:15).

translation.meaning: To shout, raise a shout of joy or alarm.
Thanksgiving; a thank offering; a choir of thanks.

gospelParallels.note: I am the gate; I am the good shepherd.

otBackground.note: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good.

overview.summary: All the earth is called to serve the LORD with gladness, to know that He made us and we are His sheep, and to enter His gates with thanksgiving, for His love endures forever.

archaeology.t: Blocked gates on the south side of the Temple Mount, where pilgrims entered in Herod’s time.
Bowls and lamps from Iron Age shrines such as Arad.

overview.discussion: “It is He who made us, and we are His” (v.3). How does belonging to God change the way I see myself today?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-100 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
